title: Normalized local Frobenius and its iterates agree with classical realization
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and write $g_Y$ for geometric Frobenius. Use the classical lisse adic categories of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], the sf raw rationalized and common-stage constructible hearts of [def-weil-constructible-heart, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and the normalized lisse realization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. Let $(M,\theta)$ be a classical lisse $\Omega$-Weil sheaf, with $\theta:g_Y^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the classical lisse pullback of [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback], and let $(K,\vartheta)$ be its normalized sf lisse heart realization with Weil structure, using the pullback and unit pinning of [def-zl-normalized-classical-weil-realization]. Identify their geometric fibres by the completed inverse-limit comparison of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. For every integer $n\geq1$ and every $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, the fibre isomorphism $c_{\bar x}:K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{\bar x}$ satisfies
$$c_{\bar x}F^{(n)}_{K,x}=F^{(n)}_{M,x}c_{\bar x},$$
where the normalized local operators are those of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], with the classical operator computed by finite-level etale pullbacks, inverse limit and rationalization. More precisely the fibre comparisons commute with the restriction-and-inverse-image-coprojection point transports along Frobenius on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, with every iterate of these transports, with the pullback-composition comparison for $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar x g_s^n$, and with the map induced by $\theta^{[n]}$ and $\vartheta^{[n]}$. These equalities are natural on Weil morphisms and compatible with coefficient extension. For every $m\geq1$, replace the base field by $\mathbf F_{q^m}$, geometric Frobenius by $g_Y^m$, and the Weil structures by $\theta^{[m]}$ and $\vartheta^{[m]}$. The same comparisons identify the new $n$-fold transports and Weil maps with the old $mn$-fold composites, so the same intertwining equation holds at every return point over $\mathbf F_{q^{mn}}$. No integrality of the Weil maps and no $k$-linearity of $g_Y$ or $g_s$ is required. The rank-zero case is included.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; natural normalized pullback and point transport, including composition, at each return period. Agent refinement for blueprint real-mixed-by-curves paragraph 1.

proof.text: Work first over a finite coefficient field $E$. The classical fibre of an integral system $M_\bullet$ is $\varprojlim_j(M_j)_{\bar x}$, and its rational fibre is its tensor product with $E$. The normalized realization datum supplies the comparison with this completed fibre. Use the SAME finite-stage realization isomorphism that occurs in its Frobenius-pinning equation when identifying the realized object with $K$; its inverse on fibres, composed with the lattice-limit comparison, is $c_{\bar x}$. Thus all subsequent comparisons have specified endpoints, rather than an independently chosen isomorphism between isomorphic vector spaces. The rational realization theorem identifies these fibres with sections of ordinary lisse module pullbacks. Its hypotheses apply to $Y$, $s$ and all their Frobenius pullbacks: they are finite-type schemes over $k$, and its scheme maps need not be $k$-linear. The completed-system data required below are supplied by the normalized datum, not asserted to exist from a definition.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text: Check the Frobenius comparison on a pulled section. In the ordinary module pullback its generator is $1\otimes u$. The ordinary-unit square in the normalized datum identifies its image with the completed rational pullback unit applied to the same section $u$. At finite quotient level the further unit equation in that datum identifies this with the canonical unit into literal automorphism reindexing. By the classical pullback definition this reindexes $(U,v,\bar u)$ as $(U,g_Yv,\bar u)$, keeping the section and the lifted geometric point. Consequently its stalk map is exactly the classical finite-level pullback-stalk map. Scalar linearity extends the equality from $1\otimes u$ to $a\otimes u$ and sums; equality can be checked on local sections before sheafification and hence after sheafification. This proves the needed one-pullback square with the actual pinned comparison, including its scalar factor $1$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text: Pass this square to the completed fibres using the completed-system comparison: reduction and inverse limit commute with module pullback, with the comparisons induced by the finite-level maps, and these comparisons satisfy identity and composition. Equality of the maps on the inverse-limit fibre follows by composing with every projection to $(M_j)_{\bar x}$; these projections are jointly injective by the definition of the limit. Tensoring with $E$ preserves the equality. The same argument applies to composites of pullbacks: both paths at each finite level send a pulled germ to its original germ, and the cited composition equations identify their endpoints. Combine this with the composition compatibility of sf lisse realization. We obtain equality of the specified classical and sf fibre pullback-composition comparisons, also for $g_Y^r$, $g_s^r$ and $\bar x$. This uses the supplied completed-fibre comparison; it does not commute an arbitrary pro-etale stalk with an inverse limit.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text:
Put $N=L\bar x^*K$. Apply the point-transport realization theorem with $h=g_s$ to each successive pullback of $N$. It identifies the sf transport with the ordinary section map
$$u/\varpi^b\longmapsto\varpi^{-b}(1\otimes\operatorname{ins}_{h}(\operatorname{res}_{h}u)).$$
Naturality of the underlying sheaf comparison makes restriction commute with that comparison; the inverse-image coprojection also commutes with a sheaf map by its defining colimit relation. By Steps 2--3, the unit in this expression and its finite reductions are the classical units. Thus this is precisely the classical transport, obtained at finite level and then by inverse limit and rationalization. The cited theorem also identifies every finite iterate on the successive pulled-back objects, with the specified composition comparisons. Hence the $I^{[r]}$ factors in the two local operators correspond, for every $r\geq1$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text:
Write $T$ for sf Frobenius pullback, $H$ for classical Frobenius pullback, and $R$ for realization. Let $d_r:T^rR(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R(H^rM)$ be the composite of the pinned one-step comparisons, using the coherent pullback-composition comparisons from Step 3. The definition of realized Weil structure gives $\vartheta=R(\theta)d_1$. Inductively
$$\vartheta^{[r]}=R(\theta^{[r]})d_r.$$
For $r=1$ this is the defining equation. For the successor, insert the inductive equation into $\vartheta^{[r+1]}=\vartheta^{[r]}T^r(\vartheta)$ and use naturality of $d_r$ on the map $\theta:HM\to M$. The result is $R(\theta^{[r]}H^r(\theta))d_{r+1}$, which is the stated formula by the recursion for $\theta^{[r+1]}$. Pulling back to $\bar x$ and taking fibres therefore identifies the final Weil-map factors of the local operators. This induction takes place in rational categories: it never requires $\theta$ or its inverse to preserve an integral lattice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text:
For $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ use the actual equality $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar xg_s^n$ in the definition of local Frobenius. Denote the three factors there by $I_K,B_K,W_K$, so $F^{(n)}_{K,x}=W_KB_KI_K$, and similarly for $M$. Let $c_0=c_{\bar x}$ and $c_1,c_2$ be the comparisons on the intermediate fibres. Step 4 gives $c_1I_K=I_Mc_0$; Step 3, applied to the two factorizations of this equal scheme map, gives $c_2B_K=B_Mc_1$; Step 5 gives $c_0W_K=W_Mc_2$. Substitution yields
$$c_0W_KB_KI_K=W_Mc_2B_KI_K=W_MB_Mc_1I_K=W_MB_MI_Mc_0.$$
This is exactly the claimed intertwining equation and supplies separately all three factor comparisons. No equality $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar x$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text: All these equations are natural in Weil morphisms. The fibre comparisons and transports are natural in sheaf maps; and for a Weil morphism $u$ the defining equation $u\theta_M=\theta_{M'}H(u)$ implies $u\theta_M^{[r]}=\theta_{M'}^{[r]}H^r(u)$ by the same successor substitution as in Step 5. No invertibility of $u$ is used. For finite coefficient extension the completed-system comparisons commute with scalar extension, the sf realization comparisons obey the scalar tower and pullback diagrams, and the point-transport theorem commutes with coefficient extension. Therefore each of the three squares in Step 6 extends to the corresponding square over the larger field, with the specified scalar associators. For algebraic coefficients represent $M$, $\theta$, its inverse and any specified Weil morphism over one common finite field. The finitely many equations hold after a further enlargement, by the directed-colimit Hom prescription. The finite-stage equations just proved are unchanged on enlargement, so descend to the actual common-stage categories and give the asserted natural $\Omega$-linear equation.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text: For the constant extension of degree $m$, identify the geometric base with the same $Y$, as in the statement. Its geometric Frobenius maps are $g_Y^m,g_s^m$. At each finite coefficient quotient, the point-transport composition theorem says that transport for $g_s^{r+1}$ is transport for $g_s^r$ followed by transport for $g_s$ on the pulled object, with the canonical compositor. Induction gives transport for $g_s^m$ as the old $m$-fold transport. The completed-system identity/composition equations pass this equality through the inverse-limit fibre and rationalization as in Step 3. Grouping $mn$ successive maps into $n$ blocks of $m$ now gives the new $n$-fold transport. Likewise expansion of the recursion gives $(\theta^{[m]})^{[n]}=\theta^{[mn]}$ and $(\vartheta^{[m]})^{[n]}=\vartheta^{[mn]}$: at the successor append the block $H^{mn}(\theta^{[m]})$, respectively $T^{mn}(\vartheta^{[m]})$. Composition coherence identifies the middle return comparison with the old $mn$-fold one. Apply Step 6 at that return period. This argument uses the iterated old normalization and therefore does not presume new independent realization data after constant extension.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Remark 6.8.15; agent calculation with the normalized realization datum, for blueprint thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraph 1

proof.text: The arguments allow zero-dimensional fibres and the zero lisse sheaf: every displayed composite is the unique map between zero fibres when the rank is zero. For $n=1$ or $m=1$ the corresponding induction is its defining base case. On the empty scheme there are no return points, so the pointwise assertions are vacuous. All maps on coefficients used above are the pinned identity coefficient maps; $g_Y$ and $g_s$ may act nontrivially on $k$, as allowed by the realization and point-transport statements.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q160-bc38e0214 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no files changed; full checks in review.md. This is a first split: the item was unsplit on base, live and side-live, there is no repair note, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. It has 9 steps and no new nodes; proof_deps equals the union of uses; there is no cycle and no SGA citation. Sources: Bhatt–Scholze Prop. 6.8.4(1),(4) and Rem. 6.8.15 checked in the local PDF; the main-20261015 thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof, paragraph 1, says the constant extension makes local Frobenius a power of the old one. Step 1 takes c_x̄ from the pinned datum def-zl together with the model-data fibre identification and the point fibres of lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization (non-k-linear maps allowed); Y is separated, finite type and Noetherian. Step 2 applies exactly the two unit pinnings of def-zl and the germ map of def-wf. Step 3 uses def-per's finite-level comparisons, identity/composition and limit projections. Step 4 uses lem-tw-lisse-point-transport-realization for any h, with its fraction formula and iterates. Step 5's induction ϑ^[r]=R(θ^[r])d_r checked, with d_{r+1}=d_r(HM)T^r(d_1). Step 6's substitution c0WBI=WBIc0 checked. Step 7: naturality without invertibility, scalar towers and common-stage descent. Step 8: Frob_{q^m}=γ^m matches h^m of lem-trf-point-transport-composition, and the block expansion θ^[mn+m]=θ^[mn]∘H^{mn}(θ^[m]) holds. Edge cases: rank 0, empty Y_0, m or n = 1, θ=ℓ with no integral inverse. Batch 5: def-per reaches only the general definition def-pod-lisse; lem-tw-lisse-point-transport-realization reaches generic iso-pullback cone normalization; lem-tw-lisse-scalar-comparison-coherence reaches generic K-flat word coherence; the directly cited lem-trf-point-transport-composition is the functoriality of the point transport (as Q96 judged). None of these is a statement or step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so all are accepted. The declared tool_uses (lem-tw-* from sk-r-real-linear, lem-trf-point-transport-composition from sk-d-weil) are accepted as generic tools. Advisory only: torsion in a classical lattice is handled by the datum's rational model and by naturality, but Steps 2–3 do not say so; the sibling lem-zl-classical-system-raw-lisse-realization also gives the I-factor; no duplicate of the item exists.
